\begin{example} \end{example}[Nonnegative scalar curvature] Source: chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-ii:page-0225 1. ch13:13.1\group Preserved Curvature Conditions

For every Ricci flow to which the scalar maximum principle applies, $R(\cdot ,t)\geq \min R(\cdot ,0)$. Nonnegative scalar curvature is both preserved and attractive. \end{example}
Proof

\sketch ↗ thm:chow-ii-scalar-wmp Since $\partial _tR=\Delta R+2|\Ric |^2\geq \Delta R$, the maximum principle gives the lower bound. Under a blow-up by $Q_i\to \infty $, it becomes $R_i\geq Q_i^{-1}\min R(0)$; hence every smooth limit has $R\geq 0$.
